question: What demonstrable and exposed downstream scientific, educational and resource consequences can presently be accounted for from the Djehutihotep derivative-image chain?
court_boundary: This run distinguishes demonstrated damage from exposed downstream dependence. The hand/rope geometric defect has been measured provisionally. The separate pouring-water feature has not yet completed wall-versus-derivative feature prosecution, so water-specific downstream nodes are exposure, not yet invalidated damage.

water_lubrication_chain.warning: These are verified propagation nodes, not a total literature count and not twelve invalidated outputs. Water-specific invalidation requires prosecution of the front figure, vessel/stream, contact point and ground/sled relation.

verified_nodes.premise_dependency: Paper opens from Egyptian tomb-drawing hypothesis, captions figure as a person pouring water onto sand, uses a rounded sled described as like the Egyptian sled, and later argues ceremonial interpretation does not seem correct in view of the experimental results.
verified_nodes.image_provenance_note: Figure 1 cites P. E. Newberry, El Bersheh: The Tomb of Tehuti-Hetep, Vol. 1 (1895), not a contemporary inspection of the surviving wall.
verified_nodes.independent_output: Measured sliding friction response of partially wetted sand under laboratory conditions.
verified_nodes.correction_lineage: 2014 shear-modulus mechanism later revised in 2020 toward penetration hardness/plastic ploughing.

verified_nodes.premise_dependency: Official release says researchers discovered Egyptians probably wetted sand and says the wall painting clearly shows a person pouring water in front of the sledge.
Reports researchers likely solved transport friction by wetting sand; quotes Bonn saying experiment solved the Egyptian mystery and uses the wall image as added evidence.
Uses modern reproduction and states worker appears to pour water; frames experiment as evidence for possible Egyptian practice.
Reports a physical sled test explicitly based on University of Amsterdam research and cites the Djehutihotep scene as evidence of water being poured on the path.
Engineering/tribology treatment of Djehutihotep transport cites Fall et al. and uses image-derived hauling configuration and lubrication parameters.
Grade-6 ELA/history lesson reproduces the Djehutihotep image and adapted Washington Post account, including the statement that the experiment solved the Egyptian mystery.
Grade-7 educator guide states engineers may have discovered the secret and says Djehutihotep imagery shows water poured to reduce friction.
Engineering review treats Fall et al. and Djehutihotep scene as lubrication evidence and carries derived friction values into later analysis.

Follow-up paper again says celebrated tomb drawing suggests water was poured to reduce friction while revising the physical mechanism from elastic modulus toward penetration hardness/plastic response.
Cognitive-psychology paper uses the Egyptian wet-sand explanation as an example of a satisfying scientific explanation, describing experiment plus wall painting as mutually consistent.
University physics teaching slides reproduce the PRL figure/caption and teach the water-on-sand Egyptian interpretation alongside the experiment.

reach_and_resource_accounting.citation_count_source: Institut Polytechnique de Paris research portal
reach_and_resource_accounting.citation_warning: 115 is reach, not 115 damaged claims. Each citing work requires dependency classification.
reach_and_resource_accounting.funding_link: Fall et al. state the work was part of FOM Programme Fundamental Aspects of Friction, financed by FOM/NWO.
reach_and_resource_accounting.FOM_budget_warning: The EUR 2.7M is the entire multi-group programme cost estimate, not the cost of the Djehutihotep sled experiment. No attributable share has yet been established.
reach_and_resource_accounting.followup_2020_funding: The 2020 wet-sand follow-up acknowledges Shell financial support (PT 67354); amount not established in this run.

excluded_from_hard_count.item: Copies labelled 2017 PSAT alternate test containing the Washington Post/Djehutihotep passage
excluded_from_hard_count.reason: The passage is readily retrievable in test copies, but official College Board provenance was not independently established in this run. It is therefore not included in the 12-node hard count.

accounting_verdict.demonstrated: A derivative geometric defect has already invalidated at least one tested downstream claim at the hand/rope feature scope and reopened two others. Separately, the wet-sand historical premise has a verified downstream network spanning research, institutional outreach, media, education and a secondary physical replication.
accounting_verdict.not_yet_demonstrated: The 12 water-chain nodes are not yet twelve damaged outputs because the water/pouring feature has not completed feature-scope provenance testing. Total worldwide downstream count, total research spend and opportunity cost remain unknown.

next_actions: Run a front-figure feature comparison between surviving wall and derivative: figure posture, vessel, alleged stream, contact point, ground line and sled relation.
Trace Figure 1 of Fall et al. through Newberry 1895 to any asserted Brown-derived ancestor.
Harvest all 115 Scopus citing works where accessible and classify each as premise-dependent, contextual-only, independent-physics, backward-historical-authority, or irrelevant to Djehutihotep.
Expand educational and media propagation with duplicate collapsing so copied stories do not masquerade as independent corroboration.
Seek grant/project records only for attributable costs; do not assign the EUR 2.7M programme budget to this experiment without evidence.
